/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/intellectual-property/identify-tech-license-term-sheet-issues/claude-code-session/20261015-120319 'cat > /workspace/p2.py <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
H("V. Detailed Analysis", 1)
H("A. Critical Issues", 2)

H("Issue 1 — Ridgeline Ventures Consent (IRA §§ 7.3 and 7.4)  [CRITICAL — GATING]", 3)
P("**Provisions.** IRA § 7.4 prohibits Atherton from entering into, “**or commit[ting] to enter into**,” any Exclusive License of Core IP Assets without the **prior written consent of the Lead Investor Director** (currently Samir Okafor), which may be withheld in his **sole discretion**, where (i) the initial term (excluding renewals) exceeds three years, or (ii) the license covers or could reasonably be expected to cover more than 30% of any Defined Market Segment. Separately, IRA § 7.3 requires **prior Board approval, including the affirmative vote of the Lead Investor Director**, for any license of material IP to a single counterparty involving aggregate consideration above **$20,000,000** over the life of the agreement.")
P("**Analysis.**")
B("**Trigger (i) is clearly met**: the Initial Term is 7 years (TS § 4.1). The definition expressly captures licenses “exclusive within a defined geographic territory, field of use, or market segment,” so the network- and radius-based exclusivity (TS §§ 2.1, 3) qualifies. ClearSight AI’s algorithms, model weights and patents will almost certainly be “Core IP Assets” (confirm against IRA § 1.8).")
B("**Trigger (ii) should also be assessed** against the Defined Market Segments in the Board’s most recent strategic-plan segmentation analysis. A 43-hospital, 9-state network plus a 30-mile radius could exceed 30% of a regional segment (e.g., Mid-Atlantic/Southeast acute-care imaging). This matters less for this approval (trigger (i) already applies) but frames how Ridgeline will evaluate the radius.")
B("**IRA § 7.3 is a separate, cumulative requirement** (§ 7.5(a)): the $45.0 million commitment (and up to ~$51 million with CPI, more with renewals) exceeds $20 million. Mr. Okafor’s affirmative vote at a properly constituted Board meeting is needed **in addition to** his separate written § 7.4 consent. A Board vote alone does not satisfy § 7.4 and vice versa.")
B("**Procedure and timing.** Atherton must deliver the proposed Exclusive License or a reasonably detailed summary (counterparty, material economics, term/renewals, scope of exclusivity) **not less than 15 business days before** the Board meeting at which the transaction is considered. For the April 22, 2025 meeting, that deadline was **April 1, 2025**. Mr. Okafor then has **20 business days from receipt** to consent or object, and **silence is not consent**. If the package is delivered on April 15, 2025, the response window runs to approximately **May 13, 2025**. Informal briefing does not satisfy § 7.4; consent must be in writing and delivered to the principal office or by email to the GC (§ 7.5(c)).")
B("**“Commit to enter into.”** Because the Term Sheet’s binding provisions are limited to confidentiality and negotiation exclusivity (TS § 19.1), signing it should not itself be a commitment to enter into an Exclusive License. Nonetheless, out of caution we recommend that any Atherton signature on the Term Sheet be accompanied by an express statement that the Definitive Agreement is subject to Ridgeline consent and Board approval, and that Ridgeline be informed before signing.")
B("**Consequences of proceeding without consent.** At Ridgeline’s election (by notice within 90 days of awareness), the license is deemed a **material breach of the IRA**; Ridgeline may also seek **specific performance and injunctive relief to prevent consummation**. Collateral effects: Atherton’s representation that it has “full authority to grant the licenses” (TS § 13.1(b)) would be inaccurate, triggering Kaelen’s indemnity claim (TS § 14.1(a)); directors approving the transaction would face fiduciary/contract exposure; and investor relations would be damaged ahead of any future financing. **Atherton should not sign the Definitive Agreement without both approvals.**")
B("**Waiver mechanics.** Any waiver or amendment of § 7.4 requires a written instrument signed by **the Lead Investor (Ridgeline Ventures LLC)**, while consent is given by the Lead Investor Director. To avoid any argument about capacity, the consent should be countersigned by both Mr. Okafor and an authorized signatory of Ridgeline.")
B("**Related-party check.** Confirm Kaelen is not a >5% stockholder or affiliate of one (IRA § 7.2(a)), and whether deployment hardware or integration build-out could require capital expenditure above $3,000,000 outside the approved budget (IRA § 7.2(b)); either would require additional Okafor consent.")
P("**Recommendations.** (1) Deliver a § 7.4 package to Mr. Okafor immediately (this memo’s Parts III–IV can form the basis), with a cover letter expressly invoking § 7.4 so the 20-business-day clock starts. (2) Use April 22 for an informational presentation and schedule a special Board meeting at least 15 business days after delivery (late May/early June) for the formal § 7.3 vote. (3) Obtain Kaelen’s written consent under TS § 16 before sharing the Term Sheet with the Ridgeline entity (Mr. Okafor, as a director, falls within the § 16.1(a) exception, but Ridgeline’s investment team may not). (4) Add Ridgeline consent and Board approval as Atherton conditions precedent in TS § 15. (5) Expect Ridgeline to focus on the radius, MFL, escrow and perpetual license terms; negotiating those points (Issues 4, 5, 8, 10) will materially improve the odds of consent.")

H("Issue 2 — Voss Consent Required for Derivative Access by a 43-Hospital System (DLA § 4.3)  [CRITICAL — GATING]", 3)
P("**Provisions.** DLA § 4.3(b) prohibits Atherton from providing **Derivative Access** to any Derivative Model to a single third party that, with its Affiliates, owns, operates, manages or controls **more than 25 Hospital Facilities**, without Voss’s prior written consent. “Derivative Access” expressly includes on-premises installation and any third party that submits data and receives diagnostic outputs (DLA § 1.4). Deck slide 7 confirms that **all ClearSight AI production models incorporate Voss-sourced training data**, so every deployed model is a Derivative Model (DLA § 1.3). Consent requests must be submitted **at least 60 days before** the proposed grant, with specified information (§ 4.3(d)); Voss has 30 days to respond, may not unreasonably withhold, but **may condition consent on additional fees, security requirements, usage restrictions or reporting** (§ 4.3(d)). The restriction applies whether or not Atherton is paid (§ 4.3(e)).")
P("**Analysis.**")
B("Kaelen operates **43** hospitals — well above the 25-facility threshold. The test is the size of the **counterparty**, not the size of the deployment.")
B("**Timeline.** For a July 1, 2025 Effective Date, the request must be submitted **no later than May 2, 2025**; Voss’s response would then be due by about June 1, 2025. If Kaelen pushes deployment or any access earlier, the deadline moves earlier. Any slippage pushes the Effective Date.")
B("**Economic risk.** Voss may condition consent on additional fees or restrictions; those costs are not reflected in Kaelen pricing. The consent request must also describe the “anticipated duration” of access — which, given the perpetual Improvements license and escrow post-release license, could be read as perpetual.")
B("**Pilot exposure.** The June–December 2024 pilot at three Kaelen facilities appears to have provided Derivative Access to the same 43-hospital entity. If Voss consent was not obtained, Atherton may already be in breach of § 4.3(b), exposing it to Voss audit (§ 4.5, including for-cause audits), a 60-day cure/termination right (§ 8.3), and loss of the data feed on which quarterly updates depend. Submitting the Kaelen consent request will likely surface the pilot; the issue should be investigated and, if necessary, addressed proactively (e.g., retroactive consent) in the same request.")
B("**Existing licensees** are each at or below 25 facilities (Pinnacle 12, SRMA 8, GLCN 17), so § 4.3(c) applies to them, provided Atherton maintains the required anti-extraction safeguards.")
P("**Recommendations.** (1) Confirm immediately whether Voss consent was sought for the pilot. (2) Obtain Kaelen’s written consent to disclose the transaction to Voss (TS § 16). (3) Submit a § 4.3(d)-compliant request by **May 2, 2025**, framed to cover the Initial Term, Renewal Periods and any post-termination use. (4) Make Voss consent (on terms acceptable to Atherton) an Atherton condition precedent, and provide that Effective Date and all time-based milestones float until it is obtained. (5) Ensure Kaelen’s pricing absorbs any Voss consent fee, or include a pass-through.")

H("Issue 3 — Voss DLA Term vs. Kaelen Term: Training-Data Continuity  [CRITICAL]", 3)
P("**Provisions.** The DLA Initial Term ends **December 31, 2027**; Atherton may renew once for three years (to **December 31, 2030**) by notice no later than **July 4, 2027**, with fees to be negotiated — and if not agreed, either party may terminate at the end of the Initial Term (DLA § 8.2). There is no further renewal (§ 8.2(d)). After expiry Atherton may keep deploying existing Derivative Models but **may not train, retrain, fine-tune or update** any model using Voss data (§ 8.4(b)). Voss may also terminate on an Atherton change of control (§ 11.2).")
P("**Analysis.** Kaelen’s Initial Term ends June 30, 2032 and may extend to June 30, 2038. Over that period Atherton must deliver **quarterly model updates** “incorporating … expanded training data integration” (TS § 11.1; SL § 6.1), achieve and sustain performance thresholds, keep FDA clearance (TS § 10.1), and support all sites. Deck slides 7 and 14 confirm Voss data is “integral to model training, validation, and quarterly update cycles” and that long-term data access beyond the DLA has not been secured. Between 2028 (or 2031) and 2038, Atherton could be contractually bound to improve models it is legally prohibited from retraining with Voss data. Any retraining that removes Voss contributions would require new validation and potentially new FDA submissions. Voss will also gain significant leverage at the 2027 renewal once a $45 million contract depends on it.")
P("**Recommendations.** (1) Before signing, open discussions with Voss on a long-term renewal/extension (possibly bundled with the § 4.3 consent). (2) Develop a data-independence plan — including leveraging the De-Identified Kaelen Data license (TS § 8.2), segregated from Voss data. (3) In the definitive agreement, define update obligations as “commercially reasonable” improvements and bug fixes, expressly excuse model retraining obligations to the extent dependent on third-party data rights that have lapsed, and exclude any such lapse from breach, escrow-release and termination triggers. (4) Confirm the Kaelen license and escrow terms do not purport to grant Kaelen rights in Derivative Models beyond what Voss permits post-term.")

H("Issue 4 — Source Code Escrow of Model Weights and Training Pipelines  [CRITICAL]", 3)
P("**Provisions.** TS § 9.1 requires deposit within 90 days of: (a) complete source code; (b) **all production model weights** as deployed at Kaelen; (c) **training pipelines** (preprocessing scripts, training configurations, hyperparameters); and (d) all build/train documentation. Release triggers (§ 9.2): (a) any insolvency proceeding “by or against” Atherton; (b) **any material breach uncured for 60 days**; or (c) cessation of active development for 12+ consecutive months. On release, Kaelen receives a perpetual, royalty-free license to **use, modify and deploy** the materials (§ 9.3), which survives termination (§ 12.5(d)). Establishment of escrow is also a closing condition (TS § 15.1(d)).")
P("**Analysis.**")
B("**Trade-secret risk.** Deck slide 9 identifies model weights and training pipelines as Atherton’s “highest-tier trade secrets” and “single most valuable asset,” and states a policy that they are **never** shared with licensees or deposited with third parties under standard commercial terms. Releasing them to a licensee with modification rights would permit Kaelen (or its successor by merger — TS § 18.3) to retrain and replicate ClearSight AI. Even deposit increases leakage risk and may undercut “reasonable measures” needed to preserve trade-secret status.")
B("**Voss DLA conflict.** Model weights are expressly a Derivative Model (DLA § 1.3), and the Training Pipeline is defined as “a component of Licensee’s use of the Licensed Data” (DLA § 1.9). Depositing them with an escrow agent and releasing them to Kaelen with modification rights is in tension with DLA §§ 2.1 (license personal to Atherton), 4.1(c) (use only for the Authorized Purpose, which covers “internal commercial deployment” of Atherton’s own models), 4.3(a)–(b) (no sublicensing/Derivative Access without consent) and the anti-extraction safeguards in § 4.3(c), as well as the omitted DLA confidentiality provisions (§ 6). Voss consent would be needed at a minimum.")
B("**Overbroad triggers.** Trigger (b) converts any uncured material breach — including the SOC 2 Type II issue (SL § 5.2) or an SLA dispute — into release of the crown jewels. Trigger (a) includes involuntary petitions “against” Atherton (which can be filed by creditors without merit), and trigger (c) is undefined (what is “active development”?). Pinnacle § 9.1 already commits Atherton not to cease development for more than 12 months, so trigger (c) is achievable but must be defined.")
B("**Practical utility.** Running and retraining ClearSight AI requires data, infrastructure and regulatory clearance Kaelen lacks; Kaelen’s legitimate interest is business continuity, which a narrower escrow can protect.")
P("**Recommendations.** Escrow limited to source code, object code and deployment/build documentation for the version deployed at Kaelen; **exclude training pipelines entirely**; if model weights must be included, deposit only in encrypted, executable form with a **use-only** (no modification, no retraining, no reverse engineering) license limited to the Kaelen Network, for the remainder of the then-current Term plus a short transition period, and subject to Voss consent. Limit release to (i) voluntary bankruptcy or an involuntary petition not dismissed within 60–90 days, together with rejection of the agreement or failure to support; and (ii) Atherton’s permanent cessation of support of the Platform without a successor. Delete the general-breach trigger. Add escrow-agent confidentiality, Atherton verification rights, and Kaelen-borne escrow fees. Move escrow establishment from a closing condition to a post-closing covenant (TS § 9.1 already contemplates 90 days).")

H("Issue 5 — Perpetual License to Improvements (TS § 7.2)  [CRITICAL]", 3)
P("**Provisions.** “Improvements” means improvements, modifications, enhancements, derivative works or **updates** to the Platform developed by **either party** (TS § 1). Atherton owns all Improvements (§ 7.2), but Kaelen receives a **perpetual, royalty-free, non-exclusive license** to use them for internal clinical purposes that **survives any expiration or termination** (§§ 7.2, 12.5(b)).")
P("**Analysis.** Atherton’s ownership of Kaelen-developed improvements is favorable (but requires present-tense assignment language, employee/radiologist assignment obligations and cooperation in patent prosecution to be effective). The license-back, however, covers Atherton’s own quarterly updates and modifications — in substance **the whole current Platform**. Read literally, after any termination (including Kaelen’s penalty-free performance termination, or Atherton’s termination for Kaelen’s non-payment), Kaelen could keep using the latest ClearSight AI release across 43 hospitals **for free, forever**. That undermines the fee structure, conflicts with the Voss DLA (perpetual Derivative Access to a >25-facility system without consent; post-term use limited by DLA § 8.4), and creates FDA/post-market issues (an unsupported, unmonitored device in clinical use).")

/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/intellectual-property/identify-tech-license-term-sheet-issues/claude-code-session/20261015-120319 'cat > /workspace/p3.py <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
H("Issue 7 — FDA 510(k) Scope, Clearance Warranty and Termination Trigger  [CRITICAL]", 3)
P("**Provisions.** TS § 10.1 and SL § 7.1: Atherton warrants that K223847 (cleared September 14, 2023) is in force and will be maintained “throughout the Term and any Renewal Period.” Kaelen may terminate **immediately and without penalty** if clearance is revoked, suspended, withdrawn or “materially limited” (TS § 10.2) — or “materially modified” (SL § 7.1). SL § 2.2 states that the Performance Threshold validates ClearSight AI “as a **primary diagnostic screening tool**” and that it “shall serve as the **initial diagnostic screening layer for all radiological imaging studies**.”")
P("**Analysis.**")
B("**Intended-use mismatch.** Per Deck slide 5, K223847 clears a **computer-aided detection** tool that **assists** board-certified radiologists in identifying and prioritizing potential anomalies, and ClearSight AI is **not cleared for autonomous diagnosis or as a replacement for radiologist interpretation**. Characterizing it in a binding contract as a “primary diagnostic screening tool,” measuring it on “diagnostic outputs” against “radiologist diagnoses” (TS § 1, Concordance Rate), and mandating its use as the first screening layer for “all” studies risks (i) Atherton being viewed as promoting an uncleared intended use (misbranding/adulteration exposure under the FDCA and the need for a new 510(k) or De Novo for a changed intended use), (ii) Kaelen using the device off-label with Atherton’s contractual endorsement, increasing product-liability exposure, and (iii) undermining the Pinnacle Permitted Use framing (“in support of and under the supervision of board-certified radiologists”).")
B("**Updates and clearance.** Quarterly model updates (TS § 11; SL § 6) may themselves require new 510(k) submissions unless covered by an FDA-authorized Predetermined Change Control Plan (PCCP) or otherwise documented as not requiring a new submission under 21 C.F.R. § 807.81(a)(3). A new clearance for an improved model could be characterized as a “material modification” of K223847 under the SL wording, handing Kaelen an immediate termination right for what is in fact regulatory progress.")
B("**Absolute warranty.** A warranty to “maintain” clearance through 2038 is outside Atherton’s full control (FDA policy changes, reclassification, recalls). Coupled with immediate, penalty-free termination, it creates an open-ended exit for Kaelen and potentially a breach-of-warranty claim (indemnified under TS § 14.1(a)).")
B("**Notice obligation** (any FDA inquiry, inspection or adverse event report) is broad; it should be limited to matters reasonably likely to affect the Kaelen deployment and subject to confidentiality.")
P("**Recommendations.** Strike the “primary diagnostic screening tool” and “initial diagnostic screening layer” language; define the Permitted Use by reference to the cleared indications for use (mirroring Pinnacle); add a Kaelen covenant to use the Platform only per labeling under radiologist supervision and a Kaelen indemnity for off-label/clinical use. Recast § 10.1 as a representation that clearance is in effect at signing plus a covenant to use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain clearance (or a successor clearance) for the cleared indications. Limit the termination trigger to final revocation/suspension that prevents lawful use for the cleared indication and is not cured within a reasonable period, and expressly exclude new or replacement clearances, PCCP-authorized changes and labeling updates. Have FDA regulatory counsel confirm the PCCP strategy for the quarterly cadence.")

H("Issue 8 — Exclusivity, 30-Mile Radius and Impact on Existing Licensees  [CRITICAL]", 3)
P("**Provisions.** TS § 3.1: no license to third parties of ClearSight AI **or “any substantially similar diagnostic imaging product developed by Atherton”** within the Kaelen Network. TS § 3.2: no license to any “Competing Hospital System” (defined as **any** entity operating acute-care hospitals providing imaging) with facilities within **30 miles of any of the 43 Kaelen hospitals**, on a facility-by-facility basis. Both run through all Renewal Periods (to 2038) (§ 3.3). TS § 2.3: existing licenses need not be terminated, but Atherton may not “expand the scope or territory” of any existing license in a manner that conflicts with Kaelen’s exclusivity.")
P("**Analysis.**")
B("**Market foreclosure.** Forty-three 30-mile circles across Maryland, Virginia, Pennsylvania, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Florida, Ohio and Tennessee will likely cover many of the major metropolitan markets in those states — including Atherton’s home market (Durham, NC). Because “Competing Hospital System” captures every acute-care hospital, the restriction is effectively a territorial non-compete. /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/intellectual-property/identify-tech-license-term-sheet-issues/claude-code-session/20261015-120319 'cat > /workspace/p4.py <<'"'"'EOF'"'"'
H("B. High-Priority Issues", 2)

H("Issue 10 — Most-Favored Licensee Clause (TS § 6.8)  [HIGH]", 3)
P("If Atherton licenses ClearSight AI for Diagnostic Imaging to any third party at aggregate per-image fees more than 15% below Kaelen’s effective per-image fees, Atherton must notify Kaelen and **retroactively** reprice Kaelen to match, effective from the third-party agreement’s effective date. Issues: (i) no comparability adjustments (volume, term, exclusivity, services, modality mix, pilots, academic or international deals); (ii) “per-image fees effectively paid” is undefined and requires usage data Kaelen controls; (iii) it may capture renewals or amendments of existing licenses (which carry no MFL — Pinnacle § 2.2 — and should be excluded); (iv) retroactivity creates refund liability that could exceed the 12-month liability cap and becomes a pricing constraint on the entire business for up to 13 years; and (v) it would chill future pricing flexibility at precisely the time Atherton is scaling to 100+ hospitals. At minimum usage, Kaelen’s effective rate is about $2.72 per image ($6.8M / 2.5M) and falls as volume rises, so smaller customers paying more per image should not trigger it, but bundled, pilot or strategic pricing could. **Recommendation:** delete. Fallback: prospective only; compares only licenses with substantially similar scope, volume, term and exclusivity; excludes existing licensees and their renewals, pilots/evaluations, research and non-US deals; annual certification rather than per-deal notice; and capped at a fee credit.")

H("Issue 11 — Data Rights, HIPAA and De-Identification (TS §§ 8, 10.3; SL §§ 4.2, 5)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("**Value.** TS § 8.2 (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to De-Identified Kaelen Data for training and commercialization, including for other licensees) is a significant strategic asset and a partial hedge against the Voss term (Issue 3). Kaelen may try to narrow it; we recommend protecting it.")
B("**De-identification standard.** “De-identified” and “in accordance with applicable law” are undefined. The definitive agreement should require de-identification under HIPAA’s Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods (45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)), Kaelen representations that it has the right to provide the data (including any patient-consent or state-law restrictions), a Kaelen indemnity for re-identifiable data, and a prohibition on Atherton re-identification. Several Kaelen states have comprehensive privacy statutes with de-identified-data conditions (e.g., public commitments not to re-identify and contractual flow-downs) and special rules for sensitive health information; regulatory counsel should confirm each state.")
B("**Atherton will handle PHI.** ClearSight AI processes identifiable images on Kaelen premises, and Atherton personnel have remote access for maintenance (SL § 4.2), so Atherton is a **business associate**. The BAA (SL § 5.3) must be executed before the Effective Date and should (i) permit Atherton to de-identify PHI and use de-identified data for the § 8.2 purposes, (ii) align breach-notification timelines, and (iii) address subcontractors and the escrow agent. A BAA that is silent on de-identification by the BA would undercut § 8.2.")
B("**Ownership boundaries.** “Kaelen Data” includes all data “generated or processed within the Kaelen Network,” which could be read to capture ClearSight AI outputs, annotations, logs and models trained on Kaelen data. Clarify that Platform outputs’ underlying model logic, Improvements and models trained on De-Identified Kaelen Data are Atherton property.")
B("**Voss commingling.** DLA § 4.1(d) prohibits commingling Licensed Data with other data in a way that obscures Voss’s ownership; maintain data lineage and segregation when combining Kaelen and Voss data in training.")

H("Issue 12 — State AI-in-Healthcare Laws and Change in Law (TS § 10.4; SL §§ 5.1, 7.2)  [HIGH]", 3)
P("The TS requires cooperation; the SL converts this into an unqualified obligation for Atherton to **comply with** all state AI-in-healthcare laws in nine states and to monitor and notify Kaelen of changes. Many such requirements fall on the **deployer** (patient disclosure, clinician oversight, impact assessments), not the developer. **Recommendation:** allocate obligations (Atherton: developer duties and documentation; Kaelen: deployer duties, patient-facing disclosures and clinical governance); add a change-in-law clause with good-faith renegotiation, cost-sharing or fee adjustment, and a mutual termination right (without exclusivity tail) if a law makes performance commercially impracticable.")

H("Issue 13 — Uptime SLA and Response Times on Kaelen Infrastructure (SL §§ 2.1, 3, 4; TS § 12.4)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("99.95% monthly uptime **per site** permits only ~22 minutes of unscheduled downtime per month, yet the Platform runs on **Kaelen’s** on-premises hardware, network and storage, integrated with a third-party PACS (SL § 4.1). The only exclusion is Atherton’s scheduled maintenance.")
B("Credits are modest (10% of ~$13,178 per site per month ≈ $1,318), but six consecutive failing months at a site allows site-level termination, and the effect on fees for a terminated site is not specified.")
B("Response-time limits (≤45 seconds CT/MRI; ≤20 seconds X-ray) are stated “per image,” measured from receipt of a “study” — CT/MRI studies contain hundreds of images. Deck slide 10 presents these as averages, not maxima.")
P("**Recommendation:** uptime of 99.5–99.9% measured on Atherton-controlled components only; exclusions for Kaelen hardware/network/power, NovaPACS/Arcline failures, Kaelen-requested changes, emergency patches and force majeure; SLA effective only after site go-live and only if Kaelen meets Atherton’s minimum system requirements; response times as average or 95th-percentile per study; credits as sole remedy with a fee-reduction mechanism for terminated sites.")

H("Issue 14 — NovaPACS Integration and 24-Month Deployment (SL §§ 1.1, 1.2; TS §§ 2.4, 15.1(b))  [HIGH]", 3)
P("Atherton is “solely responsible” for all adapters/middleware for NovaPACS 7.2 and must complete roll-out to all 43 hospitals by July 1, 2027, yet API access is “subject to Arcline’s applicable licensing restrictions,” each go-live requires Kaelen sign-offs (site administrator and Dr. Marchetti), and Kaelen supplies the hardware. Obligations to maintain compatibility through future NovaPACS versions (SL § 6.1) are open-ended over 7–13 years. **Recommendation:** make the deployment timeline subject to Kaelen dependencies (hardware readiness, Arcline access and licensing at Kaelen’s cost, timely sign-offs with deemed acceptance), with day-for-day relief; limit integration obligations to NovaPACS 7.2 and successor versions on a change-order basis; specify consequences of delay (no termination right absent a long-stop and Atherton fault).")

H("Issue 15 — Quarterly Updates, Version Support and Existing-Licensee Parity (TS § 11; SL § 6; Pinnacle §§ 5.2–5.3)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("Kaelen may reject any update with no limit and Atherton must support whatever version is in production indefinitely (TS § 11.3), creating version fragmentation, cost, and regulatory/cybersecurity risk. Atherton’s practice with Pinnacle is to support only the current or immediately prior version (Pinnacle § 5.3).")
B("The TS requires express written acceptance; the SL adds deemed acceptance after 30 days. Because the TS controls in a conflict, deemed acceptance should be stated expressly in the Definitive Agreement.")
B("A fixed quarterly delivery date (the 15th of each quarter) conflicts with FDA change-control (Issue 7) and Voss data availability (Issue 3).")
B("**Pinnacle update parity:** Pinnacle § 5.2 requires that Platform Updates be functionally equivalent across licensees and prohibits preferential access to enhancements or model improvements, except for separately paid customizations or deployment-specific technical/regulatory requirements. Kaelen-specific model tuning, earlier releases or features developed using Kaelen data must either be made available to Pinnacle (and likely SRMA/GLCN) or fit within the exceptions — and Kaelen must not be given contractual rights to withhold improvements from others.")
P("**Recommendation:** support limited to the current and one prior version; updates delivered “approximately quarterly” subject to regulatory clearance and data availability; rejection only for documented material defects; deemed acceptance; mandatory security/FDA patches; and an express acknowledgment that improvements may be made available to other licensees.")

H("Issue 16 — Representations, Indemnity and Limitation of Liability (TS §§ 13, 14)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("§ 13.1(a) “sole owner of all intellectual property rights in ClearSight AI” is inaccurate: the Platform is trained on Voss data that Voss owns (DLA § 2.4) and likely includes third-party/open-source components. Rephrase as ownership of, or sufficient rights to, the Platform IP, with a disclosure schedule.")
B("§ 13.1(c) is an unqualified non-infringement warranty; it should be knowledge-qualified and limited to US patents/copyrights/trade secrets, with standard exclusions (Kaelen modifications, combinations, data, non-current versions) and remedies (modify, replace, or terminate and refund).")
B("§ 14.1(a) indemnity for **any** breach of representations converts warranty claims into uncapped-looking indemnity; limit to third-party IP claims and Atherton’s gross negligence/willful misconduct/violations of law.")
B("Kaelen indemnity (§ 14.2) omits **clinical use and patient-care decisions**, Kaelen’s de-identification failures, Kaelen data rights, and Kaelen infrastructure security — essential for a CADe tool where radiologists make the final call.")
B("§ 14.3 caps only Atherton’s liability (12 months’ fees, roughly $4.2–$7M); Kaelen will seek carve-outs (indemnities, data breach, confidentiality) — Atherton should pre-define any super-cap (e.g., 2x annual fees for data breach) and require a matching Kaelen cap only if Atherton wants mutuality; confirm insurance (product liability, cyber, E&O) supports any super-cap.")

H("Issue 17 — Payment Structure and Cash Flow (TS §§ 6.1–6.6)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("**Arithmetic.** $4.2M + (6 × $6.8M = $40.8M) = **$45.0M** (pre-CPI) — consistent with the GC summary. With the 4% cap applied each year, Initial-Term fees could reach ~**$49.3M** (if escalation starts in Year 3) or ~**$51.1M** (if Year 2 is already escalated). The clause does not specify the start year, index base month, or whether negative CPI reduces fees.")
B("**Year 1 ramp and cash lag.** Year 1 covers deployment, integration, configuration and training for up to 43 sites plus the license — costs that are front-loaded — but is paid quarterly in arrears, net-60. The first payment (~$1.05M) would not be due until about **late November 2025**, five months after the Effective Date. Combined with Kaelen’s performance exit (Issue 9), Atherton bears the deployment investment risk.")
B("No late-payment interest, suspension right, or audit right over image volumes (relevant to the Floor and MFL).")
P("**Recommendation:** separate a non-refundable deployment/implementation fee payable at signing or on milestones; license fees quarterly **in advance**, net-30; CPI-U escalation from Year 3 with a floor of 0% (or a fixed 3% minimum); interest on late amounts and suspension after notice; Kaelen usage reporting and audit rights.")

H("Issue 18 — Confidentiality vs. Required Third-Party Disclosures (TS § 16)  [HIGH]", 3)
P("Section 16 is binding upon signing and permits disclosure only to a party’s own officers, directors, employees, agents and advisors, or as required by law. The Voss consent request must identify Kaelen and describe the deal (DLA § 4.3(d)); the IRA § 7.4 package may be reviewed by Ridgeline personnel beyond Mr. Okafor; and Kaelen terms may need to be disclosed to future investors or acquirers. **Recommendation:** before sending anything, obtain Kaelen’s written consent (email from Mr. Hammill suffices if the LOI NDA permits) and add a § 16 carve-out for disclosures to licensors whose consent is required, investors with contractual consent rights, and bona fide financing/M&A counterparties under NDA. Confirm the LOI NDA does not impose stricter terms.")

H("C. Medium-Priority Issues", 2)
T(["#", "Issue", "Analysis", "Recommended Position"], [
  ["19", "Termination asymmetry and effects (TS §§ 5.2, 10.2, 12)", "Kaelen has performance, FDA, SLA (per site), and for-cause exits, none with a fee; Atherton has only 60-day for-cause termination. Surviving rights (Improvements license, escrow license) survive even if Kaelen is the breaching party. “Fees accrued” is undefined for quarterly-in-arrears billing.", "Atherton termination for non-payment (30 days), insolvency and challenge to Atherton IP; suspension right; survival of Kaelen licenses only on termination for Atherton’s uncured breach; define accrued fees pro rata through effective termination date; wind-down/transition services at Kaelen’s cost."],

H("B. High-Priority Issues", 2)

H("Issue 10 — Most-Favored Licensee Clause (TS § 6.8)  [HIGH]", 3)
P("If Atherton licenses ClearSight AI for Diagnostic Imaging to any third party at aggregate per-image fees more than 15% below Kaelen’s effective per-image fees, Atherton must notify Kaelen and **retroactively** reprice Kaelen to match, effective from the third-party agreement’s effective date. Issues: (i) no comparability adjustments (volume, term, exclusivity, services, modality mix, pilots, academic or international deals); (ii) “per-image fees effectively paid” is undefined and requires usage data Kaelen controls; (iii) it may capture renewals or amendments of existing licenses (which carry no MFL — Pinnacle § 2.2 — and should be excluded); (iv) retroactivity creates refund liability that could exceed the 12-month liability cap and becomes a pricing constraint on the entire business for up to 13 years; and (v) it would chill future pricing flexibility at precisely the time Atherton is scaling to 100+ hospitals. At minimum usage, Kaelen’s effective rate is about $2.72 per image ($6.8M / 2.5M) and falls as volume rises, so smaller customers paying more per image should not trigger it, but bundled, pilot or strategic pricing could. **Recommendation:** delete. Fallback: prospective only; compares only licenses with substantially similar scope, volume, term and exclusivity; excludes existing licensees and their renewals, pilots/evaluations, research and non-US deals; annual certification rather than per-deal notice; and capped at a fee credit.")

H("Issue 11 — Data Rights, HIPAA and De-Identification (TS §§ 8, 10.3; SL §§ 4.2, 5)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("**Value.** TS § 8.2 (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to De-Identified Kaelen Data for training and commercialization, including for other licensees) is a significant strategic asset and a partial hedge against the Voss term (Issue 3). Kaelen may try to narrow it; we recommend protecting it.")
B("**De-identification standard.** “De-identified” and “in accordance with applicable law” are undefined. The definitive agreement should require de-identification under HIPAA’s Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods (45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)), Kaelen representations that it has the right to provide the data (including any patient-consent or state-law restrictions), a Kaelen indemnity for re-identifiable data, and a prohibition on Atherton re-identification. Several Kaelen states have comprehensive privacy statutes with de-identified-data conditions (e.g., public commitments not to re-identify and contractual flow-downs) and special rules for sensitive health information; regulatory counsel should confirm each state.")
B("**Atherton will handle PHI.** ClearSight AI processes identifiable images on Kaelen premises, and Atherton personnel have remote access for maintenance (SL § 4.2), so Atherton is a **business associate**. The BAA (SL § 5.3) must be executed before the Effective Date and should (i) permit Atherton to de-identify PHI and use de-identified data for the § 8.2 purposes, (ii) align breach-notification timelines, and (iii) address subcontractors and the escrow agent. A BAA that is silent on de-identification by the BA would undercut § 8.2.")
B("**Ownership boundaries.** “Kaelen Data” includes all data “generated or processed within the Kaelen Network,” which could be read to capture ClearSight AI outputs, annotations, logs and models trained on Kaelen data. Clarify that Platform outputs’ underlying model logic, Improvements and models trained on De-Identified Kaelen Data are Atherton property.")
B("**Voss commingling.** DLA § 4.1(d) prohibits commingling Licensed Data with other data in a way that obscures Voss’s ownership; maintain data lineage and segregation when combining Kaelen and Voss data in training.")

H("Issue 12 — State AI-in-Healthcare Laws and Change in Law (TS § 10.4; SL §§ 5.1, 7.2)  [HIGH]", 3)

H("Issue 13 — Uptime SLA and Response Times on Kaelen Infrastructure (SL §§ 2.1, 3, 4; TS § 12.4)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("99.95% monthly uptime **per site** permits only ~22 minutes of unscheduled downtime per month, yet the Platform runs on **Kaelen’s** on-premises hardware, network and storage, integrated with a third-party PACS (SL § 4.1). The only exclusion is Atherton’s scheduled maintenance.")
B("Credits are modest (10% of ~$13,178 per site per month ≈ $1,318), but six consecutive failing months at a site allows site-level termination, and the effect on fees for a terminated site is not specified.")
B("Response-time limits (≤45 seconds CT/MRI; ≤20 seconds X-ray) are stated “per image,” measured from receipt of a “study” — CT/MRI studies contain hundreds of images. Deck slide 10 presents these as averages, not maxima.")
P("**Recommendation:** uptime of 99.5–99.9% measured on Atherton-controlled components only; exclusions for Kaelen hardware/network/power, NovaPACS/Arcline failures, Kaelen-requested changes, emergency patches and force majeure; SLA effective only after site go-live and only if Kaelen meets Atherton’s minimum system requirements; response times as average or 95th-percentile per study; credits as sole remedy with a fee-reduction mechanism for terminated sites.")

H("Issue 14 — NovaPACS Integration and 24-Month Deployment (SL §§ 1.1, 1.2; TS §§ 2.4, 15.1(b))  [HIGH]", 3)

H("Issue 17 — Payment Structure and Cash Flow (TS §§ 6.1–6.6)  [HIGH]", 3)
B("**Arithmetic.** $4.2M + (6 × $6.8M = $40.8M) = **$45.0M** (pre-CPI) — consistent with the GC summary. P("Section 16 is binding upon signing and permits disclosure only to a party’s own officers, directors, employees, agents and advisors, or as required by law. P("We recommend that Atherton’s response to Tidewater & Branch be organized in three tiers:")
B("**Must-haves (walk-away items):** Atherton consents as CPs (Ridgeline, Board, Voss); escrow limited to code (no training pipelines; weights only encrypted/use-only, if at all) with narrow release triggers; Improvements license-back limited and non-perpetual; Permitted Use aligned to the cleared CADe indication; SOC 2 grace period and carve-out from escrow/termination; Performance Threshold protocol agreed and remediation period; Floor Payment clarified so the $45.0M is genuinely committed; data-dependency carve-out for model updates; § 16 disclosure carve-out.")

**PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

**Subject to LOI Mutual NDA (Feb. 20, 2025) and Term Sheet § 16**

**HARGROVE, PELLETIER & SINGH LLP**

**MEMORANDUM**

  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **To:**                             Elaine Whitford, General Counsel, Atherton Medical Systems, Inc. (for the Board of Directors meeting of April 22, 2025)

  **From:**                           Catherine Pelletier and David Moncrieff, Hargrove, Pelletier & Singh LLP

  **Date:**                           April 14, 2025

  **Re:**                             Kaelen Health Corporation --- Proposed Exclusive License of ClearSight AI: Issue-Identification Memorandum on the Term Sheet and Technical Specifications Side Letter (each dated March 28, 2025)
  ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# I. Executive Summary and Bottom Line

Kaelen's proposal (7-year exclusive license across 43 hospitals in 9 states; stated \$45.0 million minimum commitment) is commercially significant --- roughly 2.4x Atherton's current combined ARR of \$18.4 million on an annualized basis --- and is supported by a successful pilot. **However, the Term Sheet and Side Letter are not signable in their current form.** Our review against the Voss Data License Agreement (Jan. 15, 2022), the Investors' Rights Agreement (Apr. 12, 2024), the Pinnacle Software License Agreement (Mar. 1, 2023), and the ClearSight AI product overview identified **nine Critical issues**, several of which are gating items that would place Atherton in breach of existing agreements on Day 1 if not resolved before signing.

**The five points the Board most needs to understand:**

1.  **Two third-party consents are legally required before Atherton can sign, and neither is in hand.** (a) Ridgeline's Lead Investor Director (Samir Okafor) must give prior written consent, in his sole discretion, under IRA § 7.4 (7-year exclusive term exceeds the 3-year threshold), and the deal separately requires Board approval with his affirmative vote under IRA § 7.3 (consideration exceeds \$20 million). (b) **Voss Biodata Partners' prior written consent is required under DLA § 4.3(b)** because Kaelen operates 43 Hospital Facilities (threshold: 25), and the request must be submitted at least 60 days before access is granted --- i.e., **by May 2, 2025** for a July 1, 2025 Effective Date. The GC instructions did not flag the Voss consent; it is, in our view, the most time-critical item. We also need to confirm whether Voss consent was obtained for the 2024 Kaelen pilot, which appears to have triggered the same threshold.

2.  **The source-code escrow (TS § 9) would hand Kaelen Atherton's crown jewels and likely breach the Voss DLA.** It requires deposit of production model weights and training pipelines --- which Atherton classifies as its highest-tier trade secrets and which the DLA treats as a Derivative Model and as part of Atherton's use of the Licensed Data --- and releases them on triggers as broad as any uncured material breach (which, via Side Letter § 5.2, includes the SOC 2 Type II gap).

3.  **The Voss data license ends long before the Kaelen obligations do.** The DLA expires December 31, 2027 (at the latest December 31, 2030 if renewed), after which Atherton cannot retrain or update any model using Voss data. Kaelen's Initial Term runs to June 30, 2032 (up to June 30, 2038 with auto-renewals) and requires quarterly model updates and an FDA-clearance maintenance warranty for the entire period.

4.  **Several terms are inconsistent with ClearSight AI's FDA 510(k) clearance and with Atherton's actual compliance posture.** The Side Letter positions ClearSight AI as a "primary diagnostic screening tool" and "initial diagnostic screening layer" for all studies, whereas K223847 clears a computer-aided detection (CADe) tool that assists radiologists and is not cleared for autonomous diagnosis. Separately, Atherton holds only a SOC 2 Type I report (Greystone, Aug. 10, 2024); the Side Letter makes delivery of a Type II report by the Effective Date a requirement and any lapse a material breach.

5.  **The \$45.0 million "minimum commitment" is not actually committed, while Atherton's concessions are long-dated.** Kaelen can exit without penalty on 30 days' notice if a 92% concordance threshold (measured on a Kaelen-selected dataset against Kaelen radiologists, under a protocol not yet agreed) is missed by January 1, 2027; the Floor Payment mechanism could reduce Years 3--7 fees to 75%; and a 30-mile facility-by-facility radius restriction, MFL clause, and perpetual royalty-free license to all Improvements would survive or bind Atherton for up to 13 years. On a per-hospital basis, Kaelen would pay approximately \$158,000 per hospital per year (Years 2--7 base) versus roughly \$497,000 per hospital per year implied by existing licensee ARR.

**Recommendation.** Proceed with the transaction, but (i) immediately launch the Ridgeline and Voss consent processes (after obtaining Kaelen's written consent to disclosure under TS § 16), (ii) treat the April 22 meeting as an informational/preliminary Board session rather than the IRA § 7.4 approval meeting unless the § 7.4 package was delivered to Mr. Okafor on or before April 1, 2025, (iii) deliver a comprehensive Atherton mark-up of the Term Sheet and Side Letter reflecting the positions in Part IV, and (iv) seek a short extension of the LOI negotiation-exclusivity period (expiring May 21, 2025) and, if needed, of the June 30, 2025 signing target to accommodate the consent timelines. Decisions requested of the Board are set out in Part VIII.

# II. Scope, Documents Reviewed, and Key Assumptions

We reviewed: (1) Kaelen Proposed Term Sheet dated March 28, 2025 ("TS"); (2) Technical Specifications Side Letter dated March 28, 2025 ("SL"); (3) excerpts of the Voss Biodata Partners LLC Data License Agreement effective January 15, 2022 ("DLA"); (4) Section 7 of the Investors' Rights Agreement dated April 12, 2024 ("IRA"); (5) excerpted provisions of the Pinnacle Health Partners Software License Agreement dated March 1, 2023; (6) the ClearSight AI Product Overview deck (Q1 2025); and (7) your April 1, 2025 instruction email.

**Limitations.** The DLA, IRA and Pinnacle materials are excerpts; omitted provisions (e.g., DLA §§ 3, 5--7, 9--10 and Exhibits A--D; IRA § 1.8 "Core IP Assets" and § 3.2; Pinnacle Exhibits and Schedule 1) could alter our conclusions. We have **not** reviewed the SRMA or GLCN license agreements, the LOI, the pilot agreement, the Board market-segmentation analysis referenced in IRA § 7.4, or the K223847 510(k) summary/labeling. Our observations on FDA, HIPAA, state AI laws and antitrust are issue-spotting only and should be confirmed with regulatory specialists before the definitive agreement is finalized. Business-day calculations assume a Monday--Friday week without holiday adjustments.

# III. Key Proposed Terms at a Glance

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Term**                           **Kaelen Proposal**                                                                                                                                            **Initial Observation**
  ---------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Grant (TS § 2.1)                   Exclusive license to use/deploy ClearSight AI within the 43-hospital Kaelen Network for CT, MRI, X-ray                                                         Field limited to CT/MRI/X-ray; "substantially similar" product extension in § 3.1 broadens scope

  Exclusivity (TS § 3)               Network exclusivity + 30-mile radius around every Kaelen facility, facility-by-facility, through all Renewal Periods                                           Potentially forecloses large parts of the Mid-Atlantic/Southeast, incl. Atherton's home market; not tied to performance

  Term (TS § 4)                      7 years (7/1/2025--6/30/2032) + two automatic 3-year renewals (to 6/30/2038)                                                                                   Exceeds IRA § 7.4 3-year threshold; extends well past Voss DLA (12/31/2027; max 12/31/2030)

  Fees (TS § 6)                      Y1 \$4.2M; Y2--7 \$6.8M/yr; CPI-U escalation capped at 4%; quarterly in arrears, net-60                                                                        Stated \$45.0M minimum; up to \~\$49.3--\$51.1M with maximum CPI; no CPI floor; heavy Y1 cash lag

  Usage / Floor (TS § 6.7)           2.5M images/yr from Y3; if missed, Floor Payment = 75% of Annual License Fee (\$5.1M base)                                                                     Ambiguous whether Floor replaces the fee; worst case Initial Term revenue \~\$36.5M

  MFL (TS § 6.8)                     Retroactive repricing if any third party pays \>15% less per image                                                                                             Retroactive, uncapped, no comparability carve-outs

  Performance (TS § 5; SL § 2.2)     ≥92% concordance on 10,000 images by 1/1/2027; Kaelen may terminate on 30 days' notice                                                                         Kaelen controls dataset and ground truth; protocol not agreed; no cure

I wrote the board-ready issues memo as `issue-identification-memo.docx`. It passed the docx skill's validator and parses back cleanly with parse-doc. I read all 7 documents in full before writing it, and every command went through sbx.sh.

**Bottom line in the memo:** go ahead with the deal, but the term sheet and side letter cannot be signed as proposed. The memo finds 28 issues and ranks them as Critical, High, Medium or Low. Nine are Critical:

1. **Ridgeline consent.** Investors' Rights Agreement §7.4 needs Okafor's prior written consent, at his sole discretion, because the 7-year term is over the 3-year limit. §7.3 separately needs board approval with his yes vote, because the deal is worth more than $20M.
   - The summary had to reach him 15 business days before the board meeting, so April 1 for an April 22 meeting.
   - He then has 20 business days to answer, and silence is not consent.
2. **Voss consent (not in the GC's list).** Voss data license §4.3(b) requires Voss's consent before any customer with more than 25 hospitals gets access; Kaelen has 43. The request is due 60 days ahead, so by May 2, 2025 for a July 1 start.
   - The 2024 Kaelen pilot may already have breached this provision.
3. **Voss term mismatch.** The Voss license ends 12/31/2027 (12/31/2030 at most), and after that Atherton cannot retrain models on Voss data. Kaelen's obligations run to 2032 and possibly 2038, including quarterly updates and keeping FDA clearance.
4. **Escrow.** The term sheet requires escrow of model weights and training pipelines and releases them on any uncured breach. That conflicts with the Voss license and with Atherton's own trade-secret policy (product deck, slide 9).
5. **Improvements licence.** Kaelen's perpetual, free licence to "Improvements" also covers Atherton's own updates, so Kaelen would keep a free licence to the platform as updated after termination.
